name: New Zealand
sources: GDP $45bn current US$ and population 3.4m (World Bank national accounts, 1990).

Inflation 6.1%: Statistics New Zealand CPI, year to 1990, still carrying the July 1989 GST rise from 10% to 12.5%. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 had just made price stability the sole statutory objective with a 0-2% target for 1993, the first inflation-targeting mandate anywhere.
Interest rate 0.139 is the 90-day bank bill rate in early 1990; New Zealand had no published official cash rate until 1999, so the bill rate is the policy rate the Bank actually steered.

Tax 37% of GDP: total central-government revenue (The Treasury). Debt 63% of GDP is gross public debt, the peak of the borrowing left by the 1984 crisis and the Rogernomics adjustment; net debt was nearer half that.

Defence 1.7% of GDP (SIPRI). Strength 3 reflects roughly 12,000 regulars, two frigates and no independent power projection; ANZUS obligations had been suspended by the United States in 1986 over the nuclear-ships ban, leaving New Zealand formally allied only to Australia.
Oil 0.04 mbd: Maui and McKee condensate and crude, about 45,000 barrels a day (Ministry of Energy).

Separatism 0.05 is Maori sovereignty and Treaty of Waitangi claims - a live constitutional argument with no territorial secession movement behind it. Stability 62: the fourth Labour government had torn itself apart, Lange resigned in August 1989, Palmer was the second prime minister in a year and would be replaced by Moore weeks before the October 1990 election.
Investment shares: gross fixed capital formation about 20.5% of GDP, roughly 3% public and 17.5% private (Statistics New Zealand).
